title: Karin's bone-anchored, nerve-connected Mia Hand: Her phantom pain fell from 5 to 3 and her stump pain vanished, and she has used the hand daily for more than three years (Science Robotics case report)
summary: Karin, a Swedish amputee, has used a bone-anchored, nerve-linked prosthesis with a Prensilia Mia Hand daily for over three years; her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3 and her stump pain vanished.
account: Karin, a Swedish woman born in 1973, lost her right hand below the elbow in a farming accident. She received a neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis at Sahlgrenska University Hospital in a study that ran from September 2018 to April 2021. The prosthesis comprises titanium implants in the radius and ulna, and severed nerves were transferred to muscle grafts. Implanted electrodes feed an embedded controller and a Prensilia Mia Hand. The DeTOP consortium of the European Union announced the implantation on 5 February 2019. The authors of the case report measured her pain and quality of life 6 weeks before and 123 weeks after the intervention. In Science Robotics on 11 October 2023, they report that her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3 and that her stump pain vanished. They report that her quality of life rose. By then she had used the hand in daily life for more than three years, and she continues to use it.
purpose: The prosthesis was built to give reliable control, feedback and attachment after amputation, with surgical reconstruction to add myoelectric sites and treat neuropathic pain. The reported function and pain outcomes were that purpose.
system: Transradial neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis: osseointegrated titanium implants with implanted muscle and nerve electrodes, an embedded controller, and the Prensilia Mia Hand
developer: Center for Bionics and Pain Research (Chalmers University of Technology and Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Mölndal) with Integrum AB; hand by Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna and Prensilia SRL, under the EU DeTOP project
deployer: Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Sweden (surgery led by Rickard Brånemark and Paolo Sassu)
domain: Healthcare (upper-limb prosthetics and phantom limb pain)
taxonomy_note: The daily use of the nerve-linked hand for over three years is also an accessibility gain.

ratings.reason: The authors report that her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3 and that her stump pain fell from 6 to 0. Pain no longer interfered with her sleep. Her score on the EQ-5D-5L quality-of-life index rose from 0.23 to 0.63, and she had used the hand daily for more than three years. Karin says that the research “has given me a better life” and that she needs much less medication. It changed the life of one identifiable person, and the evidence comes from a single-patient study without a control group.

ai_role.statement: The benefit comes from the whole neuromusculoskeletal interface, not from a learned model alone. The paper reports that in daily life the hand ran on direct control. Signals from two implanted electrodes mapped to open and close, and a sustained open signal switched grasps. Decoding of six movements (100 percent completion) and of five individual fingers (up to 95 percent) was shown in laboratory Motion Tests. The paper never uses the words AI or machine learning. The AI framing comes from the institutions' release (Brånemark: osseointegration, reconstructive surgery, implanted electrodes “and AI”). It also comes from CNN (“AI algorithms inside the prosthesis interpret the signal”). Keep the record only if that framing is acceptable as the AI claim.

produced_by: Osseointegrated titanium implants giving skeletal attachment and a wired path from implanted electrodes to the hand
Surgical reconstruction that transfers severed nerves to free muscle grafts, adding myoelectric sites and treating neuropathic pain
A self-contained prosthesis with an embedded controller and battery that needs no external equipment, so it can be worn all day
must_hold: The fixtures must osseointegrate. Here the radial fixture failed, was removed after 5 months and reimplanted with a larger diameter
Implanted electrodes must stay within working range for years. One e-abutment screw broke after 3.5 years and was replaced
Outcomes are from one patient with no control group, so the effect size is not established beyond this case

fields.summary: Karin, a Swedish amputee, has used a bone-anchored, nerve-linked prosthesis with a Prensilia Mia Hand daily for over three years; her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3 and her stump pain vanished.
fields.account: Karin, a Swedish woman born in 1973, lost her right hand below the elbow in a farming accident. She received a neuromusculoskeletal prosthesis at Sahlgrenska University Hospital in a study that ran from September 2018 to April 2021. The prosthesis comprises titanium implants in the radius and ulna, and severed nerves were transferred to muscle grafts. Implanted electrodes feed an embedded controller and a Prensilia Mia Hand. The DeTOP consortium of the European Union announced the implantation on 5 February 2019. The authors of the case report measured her pain and quality of life 6 weeks before and 123 weeks after the intervention. In Science Robotics on 11 October 2023, they report that her phantom limb pain fell from 5 to 3 and that her stump pain vanished. They report that her quality of life rose. By then she had used the hand in daily life for more than three years, and she continues to use it.
